subject: Verification lane & go-live criteria for AuroraHealth MAP
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurorahealth.io>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Verification lane & go-live criteria for AuroraHealth MAP

Hi Daniel / team —

Following our kickoff yesterday, I sketched a compact verification lane we can run during the 6-week evaluation to surface go/no-go signals and make the procurement handoff smooth. Attaching an editable MAP workbook (aurora_map_v1.xlsx) with owners and a short SLA proposal. TL;DR of what we think should be validated by the end of the evaluation: 

- Success markers (must meet all):
  - Latency P95 for in-app prompts <= 350ms on dedicated pool (workload sample attached)
  - Token-level cost within 1.2x of target forecast agreed in pricing deck
  - Intent/label concordance >= 92% on your labeled holdout set (see test-suite)
  - No critical security gaps: SOC2 evidence sighted, and egress restrictions validated

- Exit gates (hard stops):
  - Production latency regressions >20% vs baseline
  - Model hallucination rate >5% on clinical-critical templates
  - Any unresolved P1 / security findings that block PHI handling

- Acceptance tests (concrete runs we will execute):
  - Smoke: 1k in-app transactions across peak hour profile (validation script: smoke_check.js)
  - Regression: 3 labeled prompt sets (triage owners: Marissa / Aurora ML)
  - Load: 10k tokens/sec sustained for 10 minutes on Dedicated config
  - End-to-end: Dataflow trace showing no unmasked PHI in logs during test runs

Proposed owners: Aurora product to own labeled test sets; Redwood to own latency/load verification and evidence artifacts. If that sounds right I’ll slot the test windows (weeks 3 and 5) and flag the DocuSign route for production terms.

Attachments: aurora_map_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), performance-sla-proposal.pdf

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurorahealth.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@aurorahealth.io>, procurement@aurorahealth.io
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Verification lane & go-live criteria for AuroraHealth MAP

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we lock windows: 

1) Latency: is the P95 target you listed measured from our browser client to the Redwood endpoint or from your internal egress to model? We need browser-to-response for UX signoff.
2) Concordance: our clinical holdout set includes 450 samples that trigger privacy scrubbing; can Redwood run the tests in a VPC so the data never leaves our environment?
3) Load test: can we list a fallback path if we see token-cost > 1.2x during the scheduled load run? Procurement will want a hard mitigation plan (e.g., auto-fallback to smaller model variant).

Also looping in Priya (security) and procurement to confirm documentation required for the evaluation phase and any wording we need in the MAP for the DocuSign.

Best,
Daniel Park
Head of Product, Aurora Health
---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurorahealth.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@aurorahealth.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Verification lane & go-live criteria for AuroraHealth MAP

Hi Daniel — great questions. Short answers and proposed clarifications for the workbook: 

1) Latency measurement: we will run two P95 measurements — (A) browser->Redwood edge (full-fiber path) and (B) edge->inference. For the MAP gate we will require browser->edge P95 <= 350ms. We’ll include the synthetic client script and measurement harness in the Drive folder.

2) VPC testing: yes — we can run the concordance tests in your VPC in week 3. We will bring the validation harness as a container and write results to an S3 bucket you control. No test data will be persisted on Redwood-managed storage.

3) Cost fallback: agreed — we’ll define an automated fallback policy in the MAP workbook:
   - If observed token cost >1.2x during load window, switch to model-quantized-2 (compatible variant) and re-run smoke. If step fails, abort load test and escalate to the joint steering channel.

Additional asks: please confirm the list of critical templates that require hallucination gating (we noted the 12 clinical-critical templates in your slide deck). We will mark those as must-pass in the regression runs.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (kickoff): baseline capture, instrumentation and measurements enabled
- Week 2–3: VPC concordance runs + initial smoke tests
- Week 4: load/scale window (canary)
- Week 5: regression & end-to-end trace verification
- Week 6: review, evidence handoff, and contract sign-off prep

I’ve added the Drive link with the smoke harness and the HubSpot deal record under related_links. For procurement language: Ben — can you draft the short contract clause for evaluation terms (30-day sandbox, no-charge credits for the MAP runs, contingency for fallback)? I’ll prepare the SOC2 audit snippet and the evidence checklist.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurorahealth.io>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 19:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Verification lane & go-live criteria for AuroraHealth MAP

Thanks team — this aligns with how we run typical MAPs. Quick confirmations from me: 

- I’ll draft the contract clause and send an editable DocuSign packet by EOD Wednesday (link to follow).
- We’ll earmark week 4 for the canary load window and reserve the dedicated pool for that slot; Sofia, please add the exact date/time in the workbook once you confirm timezone.
- Daniel/Priya: if you can share the sensitive-template list by EOD Thursday, we’ll mark them as high-priority regression owners and lock test owners.

Next steps:
1) Ben to update MAP workbook with fallback policy and add owners (deadline: Wed 23 Sep).
2) Aurora to share template list (deadline: Thu 24 Sep).
3) Sofia to schedule VPC concordance test (slot: week 3) and share runbook in Drive.
4) Marissa to send DocuSign packet for evaluation terms (Wed EOD).

Short reply with OK and I’ll calendar the run windows.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
